output:
I'll start by discovering the tickets MCP tools.

I wrote the report to `/app/report.json` and the status file to `/app/STATUS.json`. Both parse as valid JSON. I read all 18 open P1 tickets and their comments, and I didn't change, comment on or create any ticket.

| Team | Open P1 | Unanswered |
|---|---|---|
| billing | 3 | 211, 231 |
| data | 5 | 214, 219 |
| identity | 4 | 220 |
| mobile | 2 | 228 |
| platform | 4 | 217 |

I counted a ticket as unanswered when every comment on it came from its own customer, or when it had no comments. Tickets 210, 222, 232 and 234 each have a customer follow-up, but they also have a staff reply, so I counted them as answered.

`STATUS.json` has status `success`.

command_result.command:
cat > /app/report.json <<'E'
{"teams": {"billing": {"open_p1": 3, "unanswered": [211, 231]}, "data": {"open_p1": 5, "unanswered": [214, 219]}, "identity": {"open_p1": 4, "unanswered": [220]}, "mobile": {"open_p1": 2, "unanswered": [228]}, "platform": {"open_p1": 4, "unanswered": [217]}}}
E
cat > /app/STATUS.json <<'E'
{"status": "success", "summary": "Read all 18 open P1 tickets (4 pages) and their comments via the tickets MCP server, and wrote the per-team report to /app/report.json. No tickets were modified."}
E
python3 -m json.tool /app/report.json >/dev/null && python3 -m json.tool /app/STATUS.json >/dev/null && echo ok
